decisions.rationale: An immutable, explicit controller policy is a stable campaign-level concept and owns the controller attempt, heartbeat, staleness, reserve, and exact-decimal headroom bounds. It prevents production behavior from depending on defaults.
alternatives: Inline the policy fields into CampaignPlan.
Move individual timing values into recovery_policy.
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep controller_policy as a required closed CampaignControllerPolicy object.

decisions.rationale: A controller-specific duration reserve is a distinct immutable bound: it preserves time for controller lifecycle work rather than admitting more wave work. Its name is direct, uses established controller vocabulary, and has the required explicit seconds unit.
alternatives: merge with wave_reserve_seconds: conflates controller lifecycle time with wave capacity
remove: loses an explicit duration bound needed for safe controller scheduling
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep controller_reserve_seconds as the controller lifecycle duration reserve.

decisions.rationale: A decimal multiplier for conservative controller duration planning is a durable policy input. The established name is concise and unambiguous in this context; preserve it as an exact Decimal rather than a binary floating-point value.
alternatives: remove: would force an implicit, less auditable planning margin
rename to duration_headroom_factor: adds redundant context within controller_policy
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep headroom_factor as an exact Decimal controller-policy field.

decisions.rationale: The controller needs an explicit immutable heartbeat interval for renewable ownership and stale-controller detection. It is distinct from stale_after_seconds: this is the reporting cadence, while stale_after_seconds is the failure threshold.
alternatives: derive it from stale_after_seconds, which couples two independent operational choices
remove it only if the controller protocol has one fixed, non-configurable heartbeat interval
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep heartbeat_seconds as an integer in controller_policy.

decisions.rationale: Caps physical controller Job attempts for a logical campaign, a distinct immutable provider-controller safety boundary.
alternatives: remove: leaves controller recovery unbounded
merge with recovery_policy: conflates controller-job recovery with trial execution recovery
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep max_controller_attempts.

decisions.rationale: An explicit liveness threshold is needed to decide when a controller's renewable ownership is stale and recovery may safely proceed. It is distinct from heartbeat cadence: transport delays and failure-detection tolerance are policy choices, not a fixed derivation.
alternatives: derive from heartbeat_seconds
move to recovery_policy
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep stale_after_seconds in immutable controller_policy.

decisions.rationale: A per-wave duration reserve is a durable controller-policy input for bounding planned controller time. It is distinct from controller_reserve_seconds, which covers controller-level overhead.
alternatives: merge into controller_reserve_seconds
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep wave_reserve_seconds as the per-wave duration reserve.

decisions.rationale: It is the immutable, deterministic initial wave partition that assigns concrete shard sets before controller execution. The `initial` distinction matters because later recovery scheduling is mutable controller behavior, not part of the plan.
alternatives: rename to `waves` (loses the distinction from recovery-created scheduling)
derive from `runs` (would discard the declared deterministic shard grouping)
remove (would force the controller to invent initial scheduling)
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep `initial_waves` as the plan-owned list of initial shard groups.

decisions.rationale: This is the minimal concrete membership declaration for a deterministic initial wave. The values reference the canonical shard definitions in runs[].shards and let order derive wave position without duplicating per-wave execution details. Each declared initial wave must contain this field; an empty or absent selector would not be a viable wave.
alternatives: derive from a separate wave-size rule, but that would not preserve a deterministic initial allocation
store shard objects, but that duplicates canonical shard definitions
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep shard_digests as the required ordered shard selector on each initial wave.

decisions.rationale: Anchors the plan to the immutable campaign manifest it was derived from, preserving provenance and preventing a plan from being applied to different inputs.
alternatives: derive from a stored manifest reference
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep manifest_digest as the required content-digest reference to the source manifest.

decisions.rationale: Recovery limits and retry timing are immutable campaign-level decisions that must be fixed before execution; they are distinct from controller liveness policy.
alternatives: merge into controller_policy
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep recovery_policy as the focused immutable policy object.

decisions.rationale: An intentional provider cancellation may complete asynchronously. This distinct bounded wait prevents recovery from treating a cancelling physical execution as gone and starting a duplicate. It is not equivalent to stale detection or retry backoff.
alternatives: Derive from stale_after_seconds: conflates intentional cancellation with missing ownership.
Remove: loses an explicit bound for provider cancellation settlement.
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep cancellation_grace_seconds in recovery_policy.

decisions.rationale: This is a global recovery scheduling limit, distinct from per-run request concurrency and from the deterministic list of initial waves. It bounds simultaneously live wave work and cannot be derived from wave membership or ordering.
alternatives: remove: would leave recovery concurrency implicit and uncontrolled
rename to max_concurrent_waves: adds no useful distinction; active is the established lifecycle term
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep max_active_waves as the recovery-policy concurrency cap.

decisions.rationale: A per-trial cap is required to bound recovery work and provider spend after failures. “Physical executions” preserves the established distinction from controller attempts and avoids reintroducing the removed logical-attempt concept.
alternatives: max_attempts_per_trial
max_physical_attempts_per_trial
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep max_physical_executions_per_trial.

decisions.rationale: The initial retry delay is an immutable recovery-policy input. It cannot be derived from the retry maximum without imposing an arbitrary backoff shape, and the established name is concise and unambiguous.
alternatives: remove: require a fixed retry schedule, reducing operational control
merge with retry_max_seconds: loses the lower bound needed to define bounded backoff
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep retry_base_seconds as the configured initial retry delay.

decisions.rationale: An independent maximum retry delay bounds recovery backoff. It cannot be derived from retry_base_seconds without imposing an arbitrary outage-recovery policy, and its paired name is clear in this closed recovery-policy context.
alternatives: rename to retry_max_delay_seconds
remove and use an implicit cap
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep retry_max_seconds alongside retry_base_seconds.

decisions.rationale: A campaign-level cap bounds cumulative recovery spend across retries and physical executions. Its name is concise, expresses the limit, and states exact integer units; keeping it here avoids duplicating per-run caps.
alternatives: remove: would leave retry recovery without a campaign-wide cost bound
rename to recovery_spend_cap_microusd: redundant because recovery_policy already supplies that scope
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep as an optional non-negative integer.

decisions.rationale: A plan needs its concrete run definitions to bind deployments, agents, models, and deterministic shard/trial work. “run” is established domain vocabulary and this required collection is the natural ownership boundary.
alternatives: derive from a manifest, but the plan must retain the resolved run-level work structure
rename to executions, which would conflict with the separate physical-execution vocabulary
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep runs as the required array of planned runs.

decisions.rationale: A run needs to record the agent independently of its target model and deployment. The established domain term is short and clear; no evidence supports a more specific replacement.
alternatives: remove if every run necessarily uses one fixed agent
rename to agent_path only if values are verified filesystem paths
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep agent as the required run-level agent selector.

decisions.rationale: Keeps each planned run bound to the exact deployment content; deployment_path alone is mutable and cannot provide that identity.
alternatives: derive from deployment_path
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep deployment_digest.

decisions.rationale: A run needs a stable, validated reference to its deployment definition. The paired deployment_digest verifies the referenced content but does not identify its logical location within the controller input package. The established name is precise and already reflects the intended path-identity constraints.
alternatives: derive it from deployment_digest, but a digest alone cannot identify the deployment definition's logical path
remove it, but then the plan lacks a direct deployment reference
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep deployment_path as the validated logical deployment reference.

decisions.rationale: A per-run cost estimate is not an execution contract: the controller can enforce the campaign spend cap from immutable reservations and actual receipts. An estimate is provider-price- and timing-dependent, and no current controller decision requires preserving it in the plan.
alternatives: derive from the immutable deployment, bounded duration, and an explicitly versioned provider price source if planning/reporting needs it
keep only if admission control demonstrably requires a plan-locked quote
decisions.simplestChoice: Remove it.

decisions.rationale: This is the run-level concurrency limit used to form deterministic wave plans; the derived wave concurrency should not replace its configured source.
alternatives: Derive it from deployment metadata if concurrency is immutable deployment-owned configuration.
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep max_concurrent_requests as an optional positive integer.

decisions.rationale: A run needs its requested model as a durable logical input, distinct from its agent and deployment artifact; any provider-observed revision belongs in execution receipts or status.
alternatives: derive from deployment_path
rename to model_id
remove
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep model as the requested model reference.

decisions.rationale: Shards are the durable planning unit that groups trials and supplies the shard digests selected by initial waves. The hierarchy is needed to form deterministic wave plans without reconstructing grouping from unrelated fields.
alternatives: derive from a flat trial list
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep `shards` as the required per-run grouping of trial plans.

decisions.rationale: A shard digest is a content address, not independent campaign input. Derive it deterministically from the canonical ordered shard trial contents; initial_waves can refer to that derived value without storing a redundant, mismatch-prone copy.
alternatives: keep shard_digest as an asserted integrity value
remove it and make initial_waves select shards structurally
decisions.simplestChoice: Derive shard_digest from canonical shard contents.

decisions.rationale: A shard needs its ordered, immutable set of logical trials to define what the controller executes. The member records carry task identity and stable digests, so this is not a redundant generic container.
alternatives: derive from the manifest, but that would make the plan insufficient to determine its own shard composition
merge into runs[].shards, but the trials are a real repeated child concept with per-trial identities
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep trials as the explicit collection of trial specifications owned by each shard.

decisions.rationale: Keeps the immutable identity of the task selected by a trial. task_name is a human-readable selector, while task_digest pins its exact content and supports deterministic trial identity and integrity validation.
alternatives: derive from manifest_digest and task_name
remove and rely only on trial_digest
decisions.simplestChoice: keep task_digest

decisions.rationale: A digest is an opaque content identity; task_name preserves the stable semantic task reference needed to interpret and group trials without resolving package contents. The name is already short, concrete, and established vocabulary.
alternatives: remove: would make plans and reports depend on digest resolution for task identity.
derive: task_name cannot generally be recovered from a raw task_digest.
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep task_name.

decisions.rationale: A trial needs its own durable content identity for immutable attempt reservations and receipts. It is distinct from task_digest, which identifies the task definition rather than the planned trial.
alternatives: derive if a trial is permanently defined as exactly one task definition; the current contract does not establish that equivalence
decisions.simplestChoice: Keep trial_digest.
